I am an old man now, 67 years, and I have farmed this land many years. This plot I keep for sorghum because the rains here in Nsanje are not always good, and sorghum does not fail like maize does when the dry comes. I have no coupon for fertilizer this year, and anyway we do not put the fertilizer on sorghum like people do on maize — it is not our way, and the cost is too much for me. I will use the seed I kept from last harvest, as my father did, and I will work the plot myself with my family; maybe I will call one or two young men for the weeding if my back is paining me.
